output_list.code: function multiplier(uint256 a) constant returns (uint256 b) { b = 10; }
output_list.reason: In function multiplier function the variable b gets assigned with hard coded value of 10 and the function returns it. It can be misinterpreted as the multiple factor and then the result of the function get assigned with a value which is greater then the input parameter. An attacker may use this function to calculate a very high multiple factor which would give them enough to balance out the token distribution, leading to unfair Token Sale and even taking control of the smart contract.
